Questions & answers
How does Notion AI use my data?
We follow our standard data protection practices to keep your data encrypted and private. Notion AI will not use your data to train our models unless you opt in to a request to share your data.
Any information used to power Notion AI will be shared with AI subprocessors for the sole purpose of providing you with the Notion AI features. We specifically have contractual agreements in place with our AI subprocessors that prohibit the use of customer data to train their models. Learn more about Notion AI security and privacy practices here .
Where can I find my invoices?
Workspace admins can access, view, and download your workspace's invoices by going to Settings & members → Billing, then scrolling to Invoices. There you can click on "View invoice" to see the invoice PDF.
What are your accepted payment methods?
We currently accept all major credit and debit card brands.
What is a block?
A block is any single piece of content you add to your page, like a paragraph of text, a to-do item, an image, a code block, an embedded file, etc. Think of your page as being made up of these building blocks. Learn more about blocks here →
What happens when I go over the block storage limit on a Free Plan?
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace by yourself, you’ll be able to add as many pages and blocks as you like.
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace with multiple members, you’ll be able to add a limited number of blocks before you have to upgrade.
When you reach the limit, you can still read, edit, and organize existing content blocks as usual, but you won’t be able to add new content blocks.
Do you offer student discounts?
The Plus Plan (with a 1-member limit) is free for students and educators. Compared to the Free Plan, you’ll be able to add more guests, have access to more version history, and upload larger files.
Just sign up with your school email address and you’ll immediately gain access to these features. Thousands of school email domains are eligible, not just .edu!
For more info & FAQs, visit the Notion for Education page .
What do the different analytics tiers mean?
Basic page analytics (Free and Plus Plans): Includes a list of page viewers as well as a chart displaying views over time.
Advanced page analytics (Business Plan): Includes everything above as well as a list of page editors.
Workspace analytics (Enterprise Plan): Includes everything above as well as user level analytics, analytics on all pages in your workspace, and search analytics for content in your workspace.
How is pricing calculated for the paid plans?
If you upgrade your workspace to one of the paid plans, you will be charged a fee per member.
Guests are free of charge – but they can only access individual pages they are invited to. In other words, guests won’t be able to see all the team pages under the Teamspaces section in the left sidebar.
How do I get charged when I add members to my workspace?
When you add a new member to your workspace, they will use an existing paid seat if you have any available in your workspace. If you do not have any existing available paid seats, your count of paid seats will increase by 1. Changes in membership that occur mid-month will create prorated charges based on the amount of time remaining in the billing cycle when the paid seat was added.
For every member you delete from your workspace, you will open up 1 available paid seat. This means you have the option to exchange members in your workspace without paying any additional costs, as long as your total billable seat count remains the same.
You’ll receive an invoice for any charges accrued by changes in membership on your selected payment method, on the day of the month you initially signed up for your subscription.
Each time your billing period starts (monthly or annual), your count of paid seats will be synchronized so it exactly matches the amount of members present in your workspace.
How does adding and removing members work?
Whether you're on a monthly or yearly billing schedule, your account may be charged on a monthly basis if you make changes in membership. If you added members, your account will be charged a prorated amount based on the percentage of the billing cycle left when a user was added. If you removed members, you will not receive credit but instead will still have use of that seat for a different user for the remainder of the billing period.
How are paid seats counted?
A paid seat can be thought of as a license for one member to use your Notion workspace. Workspace owners can view the total paid seat count for their workspace by going to Settings & members > Billing. Once you have added a paid seat, you will keep it for the duration of your billing period.
When your billing cycle renews, either monthly or annually, you will be charged for your plan amount multiplied by the number of members in your workspace, plus any prorated charges for new paid seats added in the past month. Your number of paid seats will be recalculated at each renewal to match the number of members present in the workspace.
What happens when I change plans?
Upgrading your plan: Your account will be upgraded and charged immediately. The amount due will be reduced based on the percentage of the billing cycle left at the time the plan was changed.
Downgrading your plan: Your account will be downgraded at the end of your billing cycle. Learn about how your features may be impacted after a downgrade here →
How do I cancel my paid plan?
Your Notion subscription, annual or monthly, will automatically renew until you cancel it. You can cancel your subscription by going to Settings in the left-hand sidebar on a desktop computer, then selecting Billing, then Change plan. After you cancel, you’ll still have access to all the paid features until the end of your billing cycle.
Learn more about billing in this article .
What happens if my payment fails? Like if my credit card expires?
Your account email will be notified after each failed payment. Payments may be retried up to 8 times within the next month.
After this, if the payment did not succeed, your workspace will get restricted to limited-access for a period of time before being downgraded to the Free plan.
Can I change my payment method?
You can change your payment method at any time in your billing settings.
How do refunds work?
If you believe you've made a mistake signing up for a paid Notion subscription online or in-app, you can request a refund. Message support for more help with this.
We'll be happy to refund you the full amount (not pro-rated) if you downgrade your subscription within three days of signing up for monthly billing, or within 30 days of signing up for annual billing.
If you have accidentally added members to your workspace, you can remove those members at any time. If you’ve been charged for members who were accidentally added, we're happy to provide a refund of the prorated charges if you reach out within three days of the invoice date (please make sure the additional members have been removed from your workspace when writing in).
If for any reason you're unhappy with Notion, get in touch with Notion support. We'd love to hear your feedback, and will be happy to work with you to create the best experience possible.
What if I live in a region with a mandatory refund policy?
If you live in the European Union, United Kingdom, or another region with a mandatory refund policy, you may be eligible for a monthly subscription refund past 72 hours. For example, customers in the European Union can receive a full refund for a monthly subscription within 14 days of purchase, rather than 72 hours.
To request a refund, please contact us inside the app or email [email protected] . If you live in a region with a mandatory refund policy, please let us know and we'll be happy to assist you.
Still have more questions?
Learn more in our help center .

Questions & answers
How does Notion AI use my data?
We follow our standard data protection practices to keep your data encrypted and private. Notion AI will not use your data to train our models unless you opt in to a request to share your data.
Any information used to power Notion AI will be shared with AI subprocessors for the sole purpose of providing you with the Notion AI features. We specifically have contractual agreements in place with our AI subprocessors that prohibit the use of customer data to train their models. Learn more about Notion AI security and privacy practices here .
Where can I find my invoices?
Workspace admins can access, view, and download your workspace's invoices by going to Settings & members → Billing, then scrolling to Invoices. There you can click on "View invoice" to see the invoice PDF.
What are your accepted payment methods?
We currently accept all major credit and debit card brands.
What is a block?
A block is any single piece of content you add to your page, like a paragraph of text, a to-do item, an image, a code block, an embedded file, etc. Think of your page as being made up of these building blocks. Learn more about blocks here →
What happens when I go over the block storage limit on a Free Plan?
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace by yourself, you’ll be able to add as many pages and blocks as you like.
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace with multiple members, you’ll be able to add a limited number of blocks before you have to upgrade.
When you reach the limit, you can still read, edit, and organize existing content blocks as usual, but you won’t be able to add new content blocks.
Do you offer student discounts?
The Plus Plan (with a 1-member limit) is free for students and educators. Compared to the Free Plan, you’ll be able to add more guests, have access to more version history, and upload larger files.
Just sign up with your school email address and you’ll immediately gain access to these features. Thousands of school email domains are eligible, not just .edu!
For more info & FAQs, visit the Notion for Education page .
What do the different analytics tiers mean?
Basic page analytics (Free and Plus Plans): Includes a list of page viewers as well as a chart displaying views over time.
Advanced page analytics (Business Plan): Includes everything above as well as a list of page editors.
Workspace analytics (Enterprise Plan): Includes everything above as well as user level analytics, analytics on all pages in your workspace, and search analytics for content in your workspace.
How is pricing calculated for the paid plans?
If you upgrade your workspace to one of the paid plans, you will be charged a fee per member.
Guests are free of charge – but they can only access individual pages they are invited to. In other words, guests won’t be able to see all the team pages under the Teamspaces section in the left sidebar.
How do I get charged when I add members to my workspace?
When you add a new member to your workspace, they will use an existing paid seat if you have any available in your workspace. If you do not have any existing available paid seats, your count of paid seats will increase by 1. Changes in membership that occur mid-month will create prorated charges based on the amount of time remaining in the billing cycle when the paid seat was added.
For every member you delete from your workspace, you will open up 1 available paid seat. This means you have the option to exchange members in your workspace without paying any additional costs, as long as your total billable seat count remains the same.
You’ll receive an invoice for any charges accrued by changes in membership on your selected payment method, on the day of the month you initially signed up for your subscription.
Each time your billing period starts (monthly or annual), your count of paid seats will be synchronized so it exactly matches the amount of members present in your workspace.
How does adding and removing members work?
Whether you're on a monthly or yearly billing schedule, your account may be charged on a monthly basis if you make changes in membership. If you added members, your account will be charged a prorated amount based on the percentage of the billing cycle left when a user was added. If you removed members, you will not receive credit but instead will still have use of that seat for a different user for the remainder of the billing period.
How are paid seats counted?
A paid seat can be thought of as a license for one member to use your Notion workspace. Workspace owners can view the total paid seat count for their workspace by going to Settings & members > Billing. Once you have added a paid seat, you will keep it for the duration of your billing period.
When your billing cycle renews, either monthly or annually, you will be charged for your plan amount multiplied by the number of members in your workspace, plus any prorated charges for new paid seats added in the past month. Your number of paid seats will be recalculated at each renewal to match the number of members present in the workspace.
What happens when I change plans?
Upgrading your plan: Your account will be upgraded and charged immediately. The amount due will be reduced based on the percentage of the billing cycle left at the time the plan was changed.
Downgrading your plan: Your account will be downgraded at the end of your billing cycle. Learn about how your features may be impacted after a downgrade here →
How do I cancel my paid plan?
Your Notion subscription, annual or monthly, will automatically renew until you cancel it. You can cancel your subscription by going to Settings in the left-hand sidebar on a desktop computer, then selecting Billing, then Change plan. After you cancel, you’ll still have access to all the paid features until the end of your billing cycle.
Learn more about billing in this article .
What happens if my payment fails? Like if my credit card expires?
Your account email will be notified after each failed payment. Payments may be retried up to 8 times within the next month.
After this, if the payment did not succeed, your workspace will get restricted to limited-access for a period of time before being downgraded to the Free plan.
Can I change my payment method?
You can change your payment method at any time in your billing settings.
How do refunds work?
If you believe you've made a mistake signing up for a paid Notion subscription online or in-app, you can request a refund. Message support for more help with this.
We'll be happy to refund you the full amount (not pro-rated) if you downgrade your subscription within three days of signing up for monthly billing, or within 30 days of signing up for annual billing.
If you have accidentally added members to your workspace, you can remove those members at any time. If you’ve been charged for members who were accidentally added, we're happy to provide a refund of the prorated charges if you reach out within three days of the invoice date (please make sure the additional members have been removed from your workspace when writing in).
If for any reason you're unhappy with Notion, get in touch with Notion support. We'd love to hear your feedback, and will be happy to work with you to create the best experience possible.
What if I live in a region with a mandatory refund policy?
If you live in the European Union, United Kingdom, or another region with a mandatory refund policy, you may be eligible for a monthly subscription refund past 72 hours. For example, customers in the European Union can receive a full refund for a monthly subscription within 14 days of purchase, rather than 72 hours.
To request a refund, please contact us inside the app or email [email protected] . If you live in a region with a mandatory refund policy, please let us know and we'll be happy to assist you.

Proton Mail FAQ
What is Proton Mail?
View details
Proton Mail is the world’s largest end-to-end encrypted email service. Proton Mail makes sure no one can access your emails, not even Proton, by using end-to-end encryption and zero-access encryption. Proton Mail is one of the services provided by Proton. We’ve also created Proton VPN (new window) , Proton Drive , Proton Pass and Proton Calendar .
When you send an end-to-end encrypted email with Proton Mail, your message is encrypted on your device and can only be decrypted by your recipient with the corresponding encryption key. With Proton Mail, all the encryption and decryption happens in the background, meaning anyone can use encrypted email, regardless of technical ability.
Is Proton Mail free?
View details
Proton Mail will always offer a free encrypted email plan that provides secure email functionality with basic features. Our free email accounts offer the same level of encryption as any of our paid plans.
If you upgrade to one of our paid plans, you will receive advanced email features, such as additional email addresses, extra storage, custom email domains, and unlimited messages. You will also be supporting our mission to build a better internet where privacy is the default.
Is Proton Mail safe?
View details
We ensure that Proton Mail is as safe as possible by using end-to-end encryption and zero access encryption, meaning that no one — not even Proton — can read the contents of your emails.
Proton Mail data is also protected by strong Swiss privacy laws, and we can only respond to official requests from Swiss authorities. All Proton Mail apps are open source, so anyone can view their code, and we commission independent third-party experts to audit our code to ensure they are safe.
Can I create a free email account?
View details
Yes, we will always offer a free email plan for anyone who needs it. Unlike other providers, you can create a free email account with Proton Mail without sacrificing your privacy. Proton Mail Free plans are funded by those who choose to support us by subscribing to one of our paid plans.
To create your free email account with Proton Mail, you can click Get Proton for free in the table above, or go directly to our signup page . The Proton Mail Free plan comes with 500 MB of Mail storage, which you can increase up to 1 GB by completing the Get started with Proton checklist.
How can I upgrade my Proton Mail Free account?
View details
You can upgrade your Proton Mail plan at any time by logging into your account at account.proton.me and clicking Upgrade in the top right corner of your screen. From there, you can select the plan that’s right for you, depending on which advanced features you need.
How do I get Proton Calendar?
View details
When you sign up for any Proton Mail plan, you automatically get access to your own Proton Calendar . You can access Proton Calendar by going to account.proton.me/calendar or by using the app switcher in your Proton Mail inbox. If you have a Proton Mail Free plan, you will have access to 3 personal calendars, but with our Mail Plus or Proton Unlimited plans, you can use up to 25 personal calendars.
How can I expand my Proton Mail storage?
View details
Our free email plan comes with 500 MB of Mail storage. You can increase this amount to 1 GB for free by completing these simple actions from the Get started with Proton checklist:
Discover how our privacy features protect you
Set up automatic forwarding from Gmail
Change an account login to your Proton Mail address
Get the Proton Mail app on your iPhone or Android device
If you subscribe to our Mail Plus plan, you can increase your storage to 15 GB. The most storage you can receive is 3 TB, which comes with a subscription to Proton Family.
How do I switch to Proton Mail from another email provider?
View details
You can easily switch to Proton Mail from Gmail, Yahoo, and Outlook by using our Easy Switch tool. Easy Switch imports all your existing folders and messages into your new Proton Mail inbox, encrypting them the moment they arrive. Once you have completed the Easy Switch setup, your messages and folders will be imported automatically without any further input from you. The migration process happens in the background so you can continue using Proton Mail as you normally would.
Can I choose my own email address?
View details
Yes, you can choose your own email address as long as it hasn’t been taken by another user. If you’re on a paid plan, you can also send emails with a @pm.me address.
How can I access my Proton Mail inbox?
View details
You can access your Proton Mail inbox by visiting our web app at account.proton.me or downloading the Proton Mail app for iPhones or Android devices from their respective app stores. To use Proton Mail on your desktop, you can use the Proton Mail Desktop app . If you prefer to use another email client, you need to download Proton Mail Bridge , which is currently available for anyone with a paid Proton plan.

Proton Mail FAQ
What is Proton Mail?
View details
Proton Mail is the world’s largest end-to-end encrypted email service. Proton Mail makes sure no one can access your emails, not even Proton, by using end-to-end encryption and zero-access encryption. Proton Mail is one of the services provided by Proton. We’ve also created Proton VPN (new window) , Proton Drive , Proton Pass and Proton Calendar .
When you send an end-to-end encrypted email with Proton Mail, your message is encrypted on your device and can only be decrypted by your recipient with the corresponding encryption key. With Proton Mail, all the encryption and decryption happens in the background, meaning anyone can use encrypted email, regardless of technical ability.
Is Proton Mail free?
View details
Proton Mail will always offer a free encrypted email plan that provides secure email functionality with basic features. Our free email accounts offer the same level of encryption as any of our paid plans.
If you upgrade to one of our paid plans, you will receive advanced email features, such as additional email addresses, extra storage, custom email domains, and unlimited messages. You will also be supporting our mission to build a better internet where privacy is the default.
Is Proton Mail safe?
View details
We ensure that Proton Mail is as safe as possible by using end-to-end encryption and zero access encryption, meaning that no one — not even Proton — can read the contents of your emails.
Proton Mail data is also protected by strong Swiss privacy laws, and we can only respond to official requests from Swiss authorities. All Proton Mail apps are open source, so anyone can view their code, and we commission independent third-party experts to audit our code to ensure they are safe.
Can I create a free email account?
View details
Yes, we will always offer a free email plan for anyone who needs it. Unlike other providers, you can create a free email account with Proton Mail without sacrificing your privacy. Proton Mail Free plans are funded by those who choose to support us by subscribing to one of our paid plans.
To create your free email account with Proton Mail, you can click Get Proton for free in the table above, or go directly to our signup page . The Proton Mail Free plan comes with 500 MB of Mail storage, which you can increase up to 1 GB by completing the Get started with Proton checklist.
How can I upgrade my Proton Mail Free account?
View details
You can upgrade your Proton Mail plan at any time by logging into your account at account.proton.me and clicking Upgrade in the top right corner of your screen. From there, you can select the plan that’s right for you, depending on which advanced features you need.
How do I get Proton Calendar?
View details
When you sign up for any Proton Mail plan, you automatically get access to your own Proton Calendar . You can access Proton Calendar by going to account.proton.me/calendar or by using the app switcher in your Proton Mail inbox. If you have a Proton Mail Free plan, you will have access to 3 personal calendars, but with our Mail Plus or Proton Unlimited plans, you can use up to 25 personal calendars.
How can I expand my Proton Mail storage?
View details
Our free email plan comes with 500 MB of Mail storage. You can increase this amount to 1 GB for free by completing these simple actions from the Get started with Proton checklist:
Discover how our privacy features protect you

If you subscribe to our Mail Plus plan, you can increase your storage to 15 GB. The most storage you can receive is 3 TB, which comes with a subscription to Proton Family.
How do I switch to Proton Mail from another email provider?
View details
You can easily switch to Proton Mail from Gmail, Yahoo, and Outlook by using our Easy Switch tool. Easy Switch imports all your existing folders and messages into your new Proton Mail inbox, encrypting them the moment they arrive. Once you have completed the Easy Switch setup, your messages and folders will be imported automatically without any further input from you. The migration process happens in the background so you can continue using Proton Mail as you normally would.
Can I choose my own email address?
View details
Yes, you can choose your own email address as long as it hasn’t been taken by another user. If you’re on a paid plan, you can also send emails with a @pm.me address.
How can I access my Proton Mail inbox?

You can access your Proton Mail inbox by visiting our web app at account.proton.me or downloading the Proton Mail app for iPhones or Android devices from their respective app stores. To use Proton Mail on your desktop, you can use the Proton Mail Desktop app . Frequently asked questions
Free trial
Does Tailscale offer a free trial?
Yes! When you sign up for Tailscale with a custom domain, your tailnet starts with a 14-day Enterprise trial.
During the trial, you can explore all Enterprise features with unlimited users, devices, and usage, so you can evaluate Tailscale across your team and network without needing to choose a plan right away.
After the 14-day trial, you’ll need to choose a plan to continue unrestricted use of Tailscale. Before or after your trial ends, visit the Plans page to choose the plan that best fits how you're using Tailscale. Once you've selected a plan, your tailnet can continue growing, and you can make configuration changes normally.
If you need an extension, our sales team is happy to help, and we’ll talk through your options.
Personal users have access to the free tier plan for non-commercial use, which will be free forever.
What do I have access to with a free trial?
For 14 days, you have access to the full Enterprise experience, including all Enterprise features and no limits on users, devices, or usage.
You can use this time to:
Add users and devices.
Configure your tailnet.
Try advanced networking and security features.
Evaluate Tailscale with your team before choosing the plan that fits your needs.
You can choose a plan at any time during or after the trial from the Plans page.
What happens when the trial ends?
If you haven't selected a plan after 14 days, your existing tailnet keeps working. Existing users and devices remain connected, and you can continue using your network.
Until you choose a plan, however, some changes are restricted. These changes include, but are not limited to:
New users and devices cannot become active.
Pending users and devices cannot be approved.
New auth keys cannot be created.
Some device configuration and tailnet settings cannot be changed.
You can still view your configuration, remove users or devices, update Tailscale clients, and make security-related changes.
Choosing a plan restores full access to tailnet changes. Any users or devices that joined while your trial was inactive will remain pending until an administrator approves them.
Can I get a trial of a paid plan from the Personal plan?
We highly recommend signing up with a separate work email. This way, you get access to our full suite of enterprise features, which ensures you get the most out of your trial period.
If you don’t have access to a work email, our sales team is happy to help.
How do I upgrade or downgrade to a new plan?
First, make sure that you’re either the account Owner, Admin, or Billing admin for the tailnet. If you are on a monthly subscription plan or a Personal plan, you can change your plan from the Billing page of the admin console.
If you are on an annual subscription plan and would like to make any changes, our sales team is happy to help.
What is the difference between business and personal use? What determines who gets access to trials and who stays on the Personal plan?
Our Personal plan is for individuals who want to use Tailscale at home. This is a free plan and is only suitable for non-commercial use of Tailscale. It’s perfect for things like building a homelab or home VPN, playing games with friends, or securely connecting to anything from a DigitalOcean droplet to a Raspberry Pi, home security camera, Steam Deck, and more.
If you create a tailnet with a public domain, such as Gmail, Apple, or a personal GitHub account, it’s treated as personal use. These tailnets are automatically enrolled in the free Personal plan.
If you create a tailnet with a custom domain, it’s considered business use, and you’ll be automatically enrolled in a free trial. This setup is ideal for securely connecting critical infrastructure like production clusters, Kubernetes clusters, on-premises databases, and more.
I signed up with a custom domain. Can I still use Tailscale for personal use?
If you signed up with a custom domain but you're using Tailscale for personal use, you don't need an Enterprise plan.
You can choose Tailscale's generous Free plan from the Plans page and continue using Tailscale for your personal tailnet.
Do you offer discounts for non-profits or educational institutions?
Yes! Tailscale offers special pricing for eligible not-for-profit organizations and educational institutions.
To receive the discount, you’ll need documentation of your registered entity. Choose your plan on the Billing page of the admin console and reach out to our Support team—we’ll take care of applying the appropriate discount.
Seat-based pricing, devices, and resources
Why does Tailscale use a seat-based pricing model?
Our pricing model is focused on giving you more value and ensuring your bill is as predictable as possible. Previously, we charged based on monthly active users, but we heard from customers that this led to unpredictable billing.
As part of our switchover to seat-based pricing, we’ve made the free tier more generous and added meaningful new features to both the Standard and Premium plans. With the shift from our former Starter plan to the new and better Standard plan, we have slightly increased the price per seat. But even though we’ve also added more to the Premium plan, we’ve kept this price point the same.
Our goal is to give Tailscale users more value while making it easier to use Tailscale across both simple and more advanced use cases.

Questions & answers
How does Notion AI use my data?
We follow our standard data protection practices to keep your data encrypted and private. Notion AI will not use your data to train our models unless you opt in to a request to share your data.
Any information used to power Notion AI will be shared with AI subprocessors for the sole purpose of providing you with the Notion AI features. We specifically have contractual agreements in place with our AI subprocessors that prohibit the use of customer data to train their models. Learn more about Notion AI security and privacy practices here .
Where can I find my invoices?
Workspace admins can access, view, and download your workspace's invoices by going to Settings & members → Billing, then scrolling to Invoices. There you can click on "View invoice" to see the invoice PDF.
What are your accepted payment methods?
We currently accept all major credit and debit card brands.
What is a block?
A block is any single piece of content you add to your page, like a paragraph of text, a to-do item, an image, a code block, an embedded file, etc. Think of your page as being made up of these building blocks. Learn more about blocks here →
What happens when I go over the block storage limit on a Free Plan?
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace by yourself, you’ll be able to add as many pages and blocks as you like.
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace with multiple members, you’ll be able to add a limited number of blocks before you have to upgrade.
When you reach the limit, you can still read, edit, and organize existing content blocks as usual, but you won’t be able to add new content blocks.
Do you offer student discounts?
The Plus Plan (with a 1-member limit) is free for students and educators. Compared to the Free Plan, you’ll be able to add more guests, have access to more version history, and upload larger files.
Just sign up with your school email address and you’ll immediately gain access to these features. Thousands of school email domains are eligible, not just .edu!
For more info & FAQs, visit the Notion for Education page .
What do the different analytics tiers mean?
Basic page analytics (Free and Plus Plans): Includes a list of page viewers as well as a chart displaying views over time.
Advanced page analytics (Business Plan): Includes everything above as well as a list of page editors.
Workspace analytics (Enterprise Plan): Includes everything above as well as user level analytics, analytics on all pages in your workspace, and search analytics for content in your workspace.
How is pricing calculated for the paid plans?
If you upgrade your workspace to one of the paid plans, you will be charged a fee per member.
Guests are free of charge – but they can only access individual pages they are invited to. In other words, guests won’t be able to see all the team pages under the Teamspaces section in the left sidebar.
How do I get charged when I add members to my workspace?
When you add a new member to your workspace, they will use an existing paid seat if you have any available in your workspace. If you do not have any existing available paid seats, your count of paid seats will increase by 1. Changes in membership that occur mid-month will create prorated charges based on the amount of time remaining in the billing cycle when the paid seat was added.
For every member you delete from your workspace, you will open up 1 available paid seat. This means you have the option to exchange members in your workspace without paying any additional costs, as long as your total billable seat count remains the same.
You’ll receive an invoice for any charges accrued by changes in membership on your selected payment method, on the day of the month you initially signed up for your subscription.

How does Notion AI use my data?
We follow our standard data protection practices to keep your data encrypted and private. Notion AI will not use your data to train our models unless you opt in to a request to share your data.
Any information used to power Notion AI will be shared with AI subprocessors for the sole purpose of providing you with the Notion AI features. We specifically have contractual agreements in place with our AI subprocessors that prohibit the use of customer data to train their models. Learn more about Notion AI security and privacy practices here .
Where can I find my invoices?
Workspace admins can access, view, and download your workspace's invoices by going to Settings & members → Billing, then scrolling to Invoices. There you can click on "View invoice" to see the invoice PDF.
What are your accepted payment methods?
We currently accept all major credit and debit card brands.
What is a block?
A block is any single piece of content you add to your page, like a paragraph of text, a to-do item, an image, a code block, an embedded file, etc. Think of your page as being made up of these building blocks. Learn more about blocks here →
What happens when I go over the block storage limit on a Free Plan?
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace by yourself, you’ll be able to add as many pages and blocks as you like.
If you’re using a Free Plan workspace with multiple members, you’ll be able to add a limited number of blocks before you have to upgrade.
When you reach the limit, you can still read, edit, and organize existing content blocks as usual, but you won’t be able to add new content blocks.
Do you offer student discounts?
The Plus Plan (with a 1-member limit) is free for students and educators. Compared to the Free Plan, you’ll be able to add more guests, have access to more version history, and upload larger files.
Just sign up with your school email address and you’ll immediately gain access to these features. Thousands of school email domains are eligible, not just .edu!
For more info & FAQs, visit the Notion for Education page .
What do the different analytics tiers mean?
Basic page analytics (Free and Plus Plans): Includes a list of page viewers as well as a chart displaying views over time.
Advanced page analytics (Business Plan): Includes everything above as well as a list of page editors.
Workspace analytics (Enterprise Plan): Includes everything above as well as user level analytics, analytics on all pages in your workspace, and search analytics for content in your workspace.
How is pricing calculated for the paid plans?
If you upgrade your workspace to one of the paid plans, you will be charged a fee per member.
Guests are free of charge – but they can only access individual pages they are invited to. In other words, guests won’t be able to see all the team pages under the Teamspaces section in the left sidebar.
How do I get charged when I add members to my workspace?
When you add a new member to your workspace, they will use an existing paid seat if you have any available in your workspace. If you do not have any existing available paid seats, your count of paid seats will increase by 1. Changes in membership that occur mid-month will create prorated charges based on the amount of time remaining in the billing cycle when the paid seat was added.
For every member you delete from your workspace, you will open up 1 available paid seat. This means you have the option to exchange members in your workspace without paying any additional costs, as long as your total billable seat count remains the same.
You’ll receive an invoice for any charges accrued by changes in membership on your selected payment method, on the day of the month you initially signed up for your subscription.

How does Hetzner Online secure data on Storage Boxes?
Your files on Storage Boxes are safeguarded with a RAID configuration which can withstand several drive failures. Therefore, there is a relatively small chance of data being lost. Frequently Asked Questions
How does Hetzner Online secure data on Storage Boxes?
Your files on Storage Boxes are safeguarded with a RAID configuration which can withstand several drive failures. Therefore, there is a relatively small chance of data being lost. The data is not mirrored onto other servers. In addition, checksums for the individual data blocks are used to detect and correct bit errors.
Can I give other people access to my Storage Box?
You can create additional users for your Storage Box via the Hetzner Console administration interface. They can use the same protocols as the main user. Other users have access only to a designated subdirectory of the main user. However, the main user has full access to the directories of all sub-accounts.

Features
FLEXIBLE ACCESS
You can use various access protocols such as FTP, SFTP, SCP, and RSYNC so that you can easily and securely access your Storage Box. You can even integrate your Storage Box into your own file system via Webdav or Samba.
HIGH RELIABILITY
Use the Snapshots feature to take a snapshot of your Storage Box and restore it if necessary. This increases the reliability of your data. You can either create snapshots manually or have them generated automatically based on your own personal configurations.
FLEXIBLE STORAGE
Be flexible with your Storage Box. You can scale it up or down to fit your current needs, and without losing data or having to migrate it manually. Just go to your Storage Box via Hetzner Console and change to the Storage Box capacity which fits better.
Frequently Asked Questions
How does Hetzner Online secure data on Storage Boxes?
Your files on Storage Boxes are safeguarded with a RAID configuration which can withstand several drive failures. Therefore, there is a relatively small chance of data being lost. The data is not mirrored onto other servers. In addition, checksums for the individual data blocks are used to detect and correct bit errors.
Can I give other people access to my Storage Box?
You can create additional users for your Storage Box via the Hetzner Console administration interface. They can use the same protocols as the main user. Other users have access only to a designated subdirectory of the main user. However, the main user has full access to the directories of all sub-accounts.

SOURCE EXCERPT (Workiva 8-K EX-99.1 earnings release (SEC EDGAR)):
• Operating Margin: GAAP operating margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 6.8% compared to (1.5)% in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP operating margin was 18.3% compared to 12.7% in the third quarter of 2025. • GAAP Net Income: GAAP net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $19 million compared with net income of $3 million in the third quarter of 2025. GAAP net income per basic share and diluted share was $0.35, compared with net income per basic share and diluted share of $0.05 in the third quarter of 2025. • Non-GAAP Net Income: To better reflect our long-term expected tax profile and enhance period-to-period comparability, beginning with our third quarter of 2026, non-GAAP net income includes a non-GAAP provision for income taxes using a fixed long-term projected rate of 22%. This change in methodology is also retrospectively reflected in comparable prior periods presented to provide better comparability. Guidance issued prior to this quarter was prepared under the previous methodology which reflected a non-GAAP provision for income taxes that equaled our GAAP provision for income taxes. Non-GAAP net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $41 million compared with non-GAAP net income of $27 million in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP net income per basic share and diluted share for the third quarter of 2026 was $0.75 and $0.72, respectively, compared with non-GAAP net income per basic share and diluted share of $0.47 and $0.46, respectively, in the third quarter of 2025. • Operating Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow: Operating cash flow for the third quarter of 2026 was $70 million compared with $46 million for the third quarter of 2025. Free cash flow for the third quarter of 2026 was $69 million compared with $46 million in the third quarter of 2025. • Liquidity: As of September 30, 2026, Workiva had cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaling $817 million, compared with $892 million as of December 31, 2025. The remaining obligation associated with our 1.125% convertible senior notes due in 2026 was fully settled upon maturity on August 15, 2026, resulting in a $71 million cash outflow from financing activities during the period. Workiva had $702 million aggregate principal amount of 1.250% convertible senior notes due in 2028 and $13 million of finance lease obligations outstanding as of September 30, 2026. Key Metrics and Recent Business Highlights • Customers: Workiva had 6,840 customers as of September 30, 2026, a net increase of 299 customers from September 30, 2025. • Retention Rate: As of September 30, 2026, Workiva's gross retention rate was 97%, and the net retention rate was 110%. Net retention includes changes in both solutions and pricing for existing customers. • Large Contracts: As of September 30, 2026, Workiva had 2,853 customers with an annual contract value (“ACV”) of more than $100,000, up 20% from 2,372 customers at September 30, 2025. Workiva had 708 customers with an ACV of more than $300,000, up 31% from 541 customers at September 30, 2025. Workiva had 283 customers with an ACV of more than $500,000, up 20% from 236 customers at September 30, 2025. • Share Repurchase Plan: During the third quarter of 2026, Workiva purchased approximately 32.6 thousand shares for approximately $2 million under our previously disclosed $350 million repurchase plan. As of September 30, 2026, approximately $104 million remained available under the repurchase plan for future share repurchases. Financial Outlook As of November 5, 2026, Workiva is providing guidance as follows: Fourth Quarter 2026 Guidance : • Total revenue is expected to be in the range of $275 million to $278 million. • GAAP operating margin is expected to be in the range of 7.1% to 7.7%. • Non-GAAP operating margin is expected to be in the range of 19.0% to 19.5%. • GAAP net income per diluted share is expected to be in the range of $0.40 to $0.42 using 60.3 million shares. • Non-GAAP net income per diluted share is expected to be in the range of $0.78 to $0.80 using 60.3 million shares. Full Year 2026 Guidance: • Total revenue is expected to be in the range of $1.041 billion to $1.044 billion. • GAAP operating margin is expected to be in the range of 6.2% to 6.3%. • Non-GAAP operating margin is expected to be in the range of 18.2% to 18.3% . • GAAP net income per diluted share is expected to be in the range of $1.31 to $1.34 using 56.0 million shares. • Non-GAAP net income per diluted share is expected to be in the range of $2.80 to $2.83 using 61.2 million shares. • Free cash flow margin is expected to be approximately 21%. The outlook for non-GAAP net income per diluted share includes a non-GAAP provision for income taxes of 22%. Quarterly Conference Call Workiva will host a webcast today at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time to review Workiva’s financial results for the third quarter of 2026, in addition to discussing Workiva’s outlook for the fourth quarter and full year 2026. The call can be accessed by dialing 1-833-862-0080 (U.S. domestic) or 1-412-634-5870 (international). Additionally, a live webcast and replay will be available at https://investor.workiva.com/news-events/events. About Workiva Workiva Inc. (NYSE: WK) powers trust, transparency, and accountability. Accounting, finance, sustainability, risk and audit teams from more than 6,800 organizations, including over 85% of Fortune 1,000 companies rely on Workiva for their mission-critical work. We transform how customers connect data, unify processes, and empower teams in a secure, audit-ready platform. Learn more at workiva.com. Non-GAAP Financial Measures The non-GAAP adjustments referenced herein relate to the exclusion of stock-based compensation, amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, the income tax effect of non-GAAP adjustments, and in certain cases, interest expense. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP historical financial measures has been provided in Table I at the end of this press release. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP guidance has been provided in Table II at the end of this press release. Workiva believes that the use of, among other non-GAAP measures presented in this press release, non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP operating margin, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income per share, free cash flow and free cash flow margin is helpful to its investors. These measures, which are referred to as non-GAAP financial measures, are not prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States, or GAAP. Workiva’s management uses these non-GAAP financial measures as tools for financial and operational decision making and for evaluating Workiva’s own operating results over different periods of time. Non-GAAP gross profit is calculated by excluding stock-based compensation expense and amortization expense for acquisition-related intangible assets attributable to cost of revenues from gross profit. Non-GAAP income from operations is calculated by excluding stock-based compensation expense and amortization expense for acquisition-related intangible assets from income (loss) from operations. Non-GAAP operating margin is the ratio calculated by dividing non-GAAP income from operations by total revenues. Non-GAAP net income is calculated by excluding stock-based compensation expense and amortization expense for acquisition-related intangible assets from net income (loss) and adjusting for the estimated income tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments. Non-GAAP net income per basic share is calculated by dividing non-GAAP net income by basic weighted- average shares outstanding. Non-GAAP net income per diluted share is calculated by dividing non-GAAP net income, adjusted for interest expense on our convertible senior notes when dilutive and the related income tax effect, by non-GAAP diluted weighted-average shares outstanding. To better reflect our long-term expected tax profile and enhance period-to-period comparability, beginning with the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026, non-GAAP net income includes a non-GAAP provision for income taxes of 22%, which was not included in our previously-issued guidance. This change is also retrospectively reflected in comparable prior periods presented. Previously, our non-GAAP provision for income taxes equaled our GAAP provision for income taxes. The rate presented is based on a three-year financial projection that excludes the direct impact of non-GAAP adjustments, assumes no benefit from available U.S. net operating loss or tax credit carryforwards or valuation allowances, considers our operating structure, jurisdictional tax positions and key tax legislation, and differs from our GAAP effective tax rate. We re-evaluate the rate periodically for significant events, tax law changes, and material changes in geographic earnings mix. Moreover, beginning with the three months and six months ended June 30, 2026, we are adding back interest expense to the numerator of our non-GAAP diluted earnings per share in accordance with the if-converted method of calculating the dilutive impact of our convertible senior notes with the related income tax effect presented separately within the income tax effect of non-GAAP adjustments. Prior to this change, potentially dilutive shares associated with our convertible senior notes were included in the denominator, but the numerator was not adjusted, as our convertible senior notes had historically been anti-dilutive for GAAP purposes. As Workiva has achieved GAAP profitability, our convertible senior notes may now be dilutive, and we are aligning our non-GAAP calculation with the if-converted method used for GAAP diluted earnings per share. Prior periods have been recast for comparative purposes. Because of varying available valuation methodologies, subjective assumptions and the variety of equity instruments that can impact a company’s non-cash expenses, Workiva believes that providing non-GAAP financial measures that exclude stock-based compensation expense allows for more meaningful comparisons between its operating results from period to period. For business combinations, we generally allocate a portion of the purchase price to intangible assets. The amount of the allocation is based on estimates and assumptions made by management and is subject to amortization. The amount of purchase price allocated to intangible assets and the term of its related amortization can vary significantly and are unique to each acquisition and thus we do not believe they are reflective of ongoing operations. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, represents cash flow from operating activities less purchases of property and equipment. Free cash flow margin is calculated by dividing free cash flow by total revenue. We consider free cash flow and free cash flow margin to be liquidity measures that provide useful information to investors about the amount of cash generated or used by the business. The utility of free cash flow and free cash flow margin as measures of our liquidity is limited because these measures do not represent the total increase or decrease in our cash balance for a given period. Non-GAAP financial measures may not provide information that is directly comparable to that provided by other companies in Workiva’s industry, as other companies in the industry may calculate non-GAAP financial results differently. In addition, there are limitations in using non-GAAP financial measures because the non-GAAP financial measures are not prepared in accordance with GAAP, may be different from non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies and exclude expenses that may have a material impact on Workiva’s reported financial results. Further, stock-based compensation expense has been and will continue to be for the foreseeable future a significant recurring expense in Workiva’s business and an important part of the compensation provided to its employees.

 EX-99.1 2 prlb-20261029xexx991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Protolabs Reports Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026 Record Quarterly Revenue of $154.3 Million, a 14.0% Increase Year-Over-Year GAAP Earnings Per Share of $0.48, up 61% YoY; Non-GAAP Earnings Per Share of $0.63, up 33% YoY Raising Full Year 2026 Revenue Growth Guidance from 8% - 10% to 10% - 11% MINNEAPOLIS – October 29, 2026 – Proto Labs, Inc. ("Protolabs" or the "Company") (NYSE: PRLB), the world’s leading provider of digital manufacturing services, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights : • Revenue was a record $154.3 million, a 14.0% increase over the third quarter of 2025. ◦ Total revenue per customer contact increased 16.6% year-over-year. ◦ CNC machining revenue grew 16.4% year-over-year. ◦ Injection molding revenue grew 12.5% year-over-year. ◦ 3D printing revenue grew 11.4% year-over-year. • GAAP operating margin was 9.4%, up from 6.5% in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP operating margin was 11.9%, up from 10.0% in the third quarter of 2025. • GAAP net income was $0.48 per diluted share, compared to $0.30 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP net income was $0.63 per diluted share, compared to $0.47 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025. Note: See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. "Protolabs delivered another record quarter, with double-digit revenue growth for the fourth consecutive quarter," said Suresh Krishna, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Our momentum reflects strong execution and growing demand from industries that value speed, quality, and manufacturing agility. As reindustrialization, advanced hardware innovation, and the need for resilient supply chains reshape manufacturing, our digital model enables customers to move quickly from idea to production — positioning us to deliver sustained profitable growth and long-term shareholder value." Additional Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights : • GAAP net income was $11.8 million, or 7.6% of revenue, up 63.0% compared to $7.2 million, or 5.3% of revenue in the third quarter of 2025. • Adjusted EBITDA was $26.2 million, or 17.0% of revenue, up 23.8% compared to $21.1 million, or 15.6% of revenue, in the third quarter of 2025. See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. • Cash generated from operations was $22.8 million. • Cash and investments balance was $175.0 million as of September 30, 2026. "We delivered another quarter of strong financial performance, with broad-based revenue growth, meaningful operating leverage, and continued earnings growth," said Dan Schumacher, Chief Financial Officer. "We remain focused on balancing investments in our strategic priorities with disciplined cost management, while generating strong cash flow and positioning the business for sustained profitable growth." Financial Guidance and Outlook: • For full year 2026, Protolabs is raising its guidance and now expects revenue growth between 10% and 11%. • For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects revenue between $143.0 million and $151.0 million. • For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects GAAP diluted net income per share between $0.28 and $0.36, and non-GAAP diluted net income per share between $0.46 and $0.54. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" below. Non-GAAP Financial Measures The Company has included non-GAAP revenue growth by region and by product line that excludes the impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates (collectively, “non-GAAP revenue growth”). Management believes these metrics, when viewed in conjunction with the comparable metrics calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States ("GAAP"), are useful in evaluating the underlying business trends and ongoing operating performance of the Company. The Company has included earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (“EBITDA”) and EBITDA, adjusted for stock-based compensation expense, unrealized loss (gain) on foreign currency, trade refunds and charges, net, restructuring and transformation costs, costs related to exit and disposal activities and CEO transition costs (collectively, “Adjusted EBITDA”), in this press release to provide investors with additional information regarding the Company’s financial results. The Company has also included earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization margin (“EBITDA margin”) and EBITDA margin, adjusted for stock-based compensation expense, unrealized loss (gain) on foreign currency, trade refunds and charges, net, restructuring and transformation costs, costs related to exit and disposal activities and CEO transition costs (“Adjusted EBITDA margin”), in this press release to provide investors with additional information regarding the Company’s financial results. The Company has included non-GAAP gross margin, adjusted for stock-based compensation expense, amortization expense and trade refunds and charges, net ("non-GAAP gross margin"), in this press release to provide investors with additional information regarding the Company’s financial results. The Company has included non-GAAP operating margin, adjusted for stock-based compensation expense, amortization expense, trade refunds and charges, net, restructuring and transformation costs, costs related to exit and disposal activities and CEO transition costs (“non-GAAP operating margin”), in this press release to provide investors with additional information regarding the Company’s financial results. Non-GAAP net income was $0.63 per diluted share, compared to $0.47 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025. Note: See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. "Protolabs delivered another record quarter, with double-digit revenue growth for the fourth consecutive quarter," said Suresh Krishna, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Our momentum reflects strong execution and growing demand from industries that value speed, quality, and manufacturing agility. As reindustrialization, advanced hardware innovation, and the need for resilient supply chains reshape manufacturing, our digital model enables customers to move quickly from idea to production — positioning us to deliver sustained profitable growth and long-term shareholder value." Additional Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights : • GAAP net income was $11.8 million, or 7.6% of revenue, up 63.0% compared to $7.2 million, or 5.3% of revenue in the third quarter of 2025. • Adjusted EBITDA was $26.2 million, or 17.0% of revenue, up 23.8% compared to $21.1 million, or 15.6% of revenue, in the third quarter of 2025. See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. • Cash generated from operations was $22.8 million. • Cash and investments balance was $175.0 million as of September 30, 2026. "We delivered another quarter of strong financial performance, with broad-based revenue growth, meaningful operating leverage, and continued earnings growth," said Dan Schumacher, Chief Financial Officer. Non-GAAP operating margin was 11.9%, up from 10.0% in the third quarter of 2025. • GAAP net income was $0.48 per diluted share, compared to $0.30 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP net income was $0.63 per diluted share, compared to $0.47 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025. Note: See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. "Protolabs delivered another record quarter, with double-digit revenue growth for the fourth consecutive quarter," said Suresh Krishna, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Our momentum reflects strong execution and growing demand from industries that value speed, quality, and manufacturing agility. As reindustrialization, advanced hardware innovation, and the need for resilient supply chains reshape manufacturing, our digital model enables customers to move quickly from idea to production — positioning us to deliver sustained profitable growth and long-term shareholder value." Additional Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights : • GAAP net income was $11.8 million, or 7.6% of revenue, up 63.0% compared to $7.2 million, or 5.3% of revenue in the third quarter of 2025. • Adjusted EBITDA was $26.2 million, or 17.0% of revenue, up 23.8% compared to $21.1 million, or 15.6% of revenue, in the third quarter of 2025. See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. • Cash generated from operations was $22.8 million. • Cash and investments balance was $175.0 million as of September 30, 2026. "We delivered another quarter of strong financial performance, with broad-based revenue growth, meaningful operating leverage, and continued earnings growth," said Dan Schumacher, Chief Financial Officer. "We remain focused on balancing investments in our strategic priorities with disciplined cost management, while generating strong cash flow and positioning the business for sustained profitable growth." Financial Guidance and Outlook: • For full year 2026, Protolabs is raising its guidance and now expects revenue growth between 10% and 11%. • For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects revenue between $143.0 million and $151.0 million. • For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects GAAP diluted net income per share between $0.28 and $0.36, and non-GAAP diluted net income per share between $0.46 and $0.54. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" below.
